channel.title: Deep Press Analysis
channel.description: Independent analysis of corporate power, financial systems, geopolitical risk, global governance, and the infrastructure shaping economic and strategic dependencies.

item.title: Press Narratives and Institutional Power
item.description: Four institutional narratives emerge from November 24 press coverage and related policy documents: U.S. intervention in AI-sector governance, security arguments surrounding a reported Russian nuclear-capable satellite, British proposals to restructure independent regulators and youth benefits, and European efforts to prioritize domestic quantum technologies while reconsidering consensus rules in climate diplomacy.

item.title: 2027 Outlook: Geopolitics, AI and Debt: A 2027 outlook informed by The Economist’s special edition
item.description: A 2027 outlook informed by The Economist’s special edition: the political aftermath of the US midterms, the geopolitical and financial consequences of accelerating artificial intelligence, pressure on sovereign borrowing, unresolved conflicts involving Iran and Ukraine, and uncertainty over Taiwan, energy, and climate.

item.title: Geopolitics, AI, and the 2027 Outlook: The Economist examines growing cooperation among China
item.description: The Economist examines growing cooperation among China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea; the challenges facing American semiconductor controls and digital infrastructure; the post-midterm political transition in Washington; banking stress in Bangladesh and fiscal pressures across major economies; and competing scenarios for artificial intelligence and global power in 2027.

item.title: Inflation Shock and Treasury Sell-Off Risks
item.description: An evaluation of the likelihood and causal pathways of a renewed U.S. inflation shock paired with a Treasury bond sell-off, assessing energy supply disruptions, fiscal stimulus, and monetary policy missteps alongside Monte Carlo risk simulations and critical market indicators.

item.title: Shenzhen Summit and Global Power Limits: The Shenzhen leaders’ declaration contrasts with reported
item.description: The Shenzhen leaders’ declaration contrasts with reported defense-production bottlenecks, the wars in Ukraine and Iran, and shifts in energy and sovereign borrowing. The investigation follows record AI fundraising, financing and electricity constraints, and disputed legal and institutional developments in Israel, the United States, and the wider region.

item.title: France’s Sovereign Debt and Euro-Area Contagion
item.description: France’s widening sovereign risk premium is analyzed against a 300-basis-point OAT–Bund stress threshold. The report evaluates debt refinancing, political constraints, the ECB’s conditional intervention tools, 1.5 million simulated market paths, and possible spillovers to Belgian and Italian debt.

item.title: U.S. AI Chip Export Controls and Remote Compute
item.description: The November 9 BIS extension temporarily stays expanded affiliate-based export controls through January 10, 2027, while a BIS interim final rule scheduled for November 19 targets remote access to advanced computing and chip shipments to five diversion-risk countries. The issue examines licensing thresholds, cloud and semiconductor supply chains, company exposure, and near-term regulatory deadlines.

item.title: NVIDIA, AI Governance, and Corporate Power
item.description: Six newspapers frame NVIDIA’s leadership transition and U.S. chip-access restrictions through different political, financial, and security lenses. The investigation also compares AI-service metrics, alleged cloud surveillance, data-center energy priorities, and disclosed sponsorship.

item.title: AI Compute, Chip Controls, and UK Welfare
item.description: A comparative analysis of The Guardian and Financial Times (US edition, November 16, 2026) highlights a structural shift from open, low-cost access toward conditional allocation across AI compute, power grids, and public welfare. While data-center suppliers lost $4.2 trillion in market value amid scrutiny of capital returns, hyperscaler capital expenditures exceeding $700 billion in 2026 and physical grid bottlenecks sustain underlying infrastructure demand alongside tightening US semiconductor export controls and UK labor-market reforms.

item.title: AI Sector Crash and Nasdaq Contagion: The artificial intelligence sector stands at a critical…
item.description: The artificial intelligence sector stands at a critical phase transition, where Nvidia's localized stock correction, exacerbated by an unprecedented corporate governance crisis, risks escalating into a structural capital cycle crash that could trigger a cascading contagion across the Nasdaq-100.

item.title: Defense Supply Chain and Cascade Risks: A fundamental structural shift in the architecture of the…
item.description: A fundamental structural shift in the architecture of the Western military-industrial and technological complex, driven by direct government equity buyouts, strategic capital loans, and forced allocation orders targeting critical raw materials and Tier-2/Tier-3 supply chain bottlenecks.

item.title: Nvidia Crisis, AI Debt, and Global Shifts
item.description: Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia amid the Megaspeed export control investigation exposes structural vulnerabilities in circular artificial intelligence financing and corporate debt limits. Simultaneously, Democratic victories in the 2026 US midterm elections, driven by inflation, energy costs, and local resistance to data centers, coincide with intensified diplomatic and military pressures across the Middle East, Ukraine, and the Asia-Pacific.

item.title: Insider Buys, Export Controls & Defense Flows
item.description: An analytical early-detection report examining open-market insider purchases in semiconductors, AI data centers, energy, and biotech alongside U.S. outbound investment restrictions (31 CFR Part 851), major defense and cyber contracts, and institutional 13F/10-Q portfolio rotations.

item.title: State Procurement of AI Surveillance and Algorithmic Control
item.description: A systemic analysis of federal tenders in the US and EU during 2024-2026, revealing a structural shift toward the procurement of integrated AI surveillance, multimodal biometrics, and algorithmic control architectures.
